IcgmSRJHu_8.summary: Richard Feldman's elm-conf talk on designing models so that bugs from impossible application states cannot occur, using Elm's compiler and types. It demonstrates techniques for making invalid states unrepresentable.
IcgmSRJHu_8.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as a talk that changed how people model data, with ideas that apply well beyond Elm to any typed language.

Ik1AK56FtVc.summary: Lawrence Lessig's Talks at Google presentation based on his book Republic, Lost, arguing that money in politics corrupts Congress and eroded public trust, and outlining what could be done about it. It supports the argument with data on political donations.
Ik1AK56FtVc.why: A perennial HN recommendation whenever lobbying, SOPA, taxes or political corruption come up, with several commenters saying it changed their views.

IlU-zDU6aQ0.summary: Psychology professor Marty Lobdell gives a one-hour lecture on how to study effectively, covering short focused sessions with breaks, study environment, note-taking and memory techniques. It was aimed at students who cram without improving.
IlU-zDU6aQ0.why: HN recommends it for productivity, focus and working-from-home threads, since its advice on breaks and mental modes applies beyond studying.

I8LbkfSSR58.summary: The first lecture in Bartosz Milewski's category theory series for programmers. It covers the motivation and philosophy behind category theory and why composition matters for handling complexity.
I8LbkfSSR58.why: HN commenters repeatedly name it as the friendliest entry point to category theory for working programmers.

IOiZatlZtGU.summary: Philip Wadler's Strange Loop talk on Propositions as Types, the link between logic and computation (the Curry-Howard correspondence). He traces its history through Church, Godel and Turing and shows how it shaped theorem provers and programming languages.
IOiZatlZtGU.why: HN regards it as an entertaining and eye-opening introduction to why logic and functional programming are connected, and it is a frequent pick in favorite-tech-talk threads.

I8Xc2_FtpHI.summary: The first lecture of Jordan Peterson's 2017 Maps of Meaning course, setting out the Cold War context for his theory of belief and culture. He introduces the narrative structure of culture and archetypal characters for the individual, the known and the unknown.
I8Xc2_FtpHI.why: Several HN commenters credit the lecture series with helping them through depression or personal collapse and recommend it as long-form learning.

Ip3X9LOh2dk.summary: A 10-minute 3Blue1Brown chapter explaining the determinant as the factor by which a linear transformation scales area or volume. It builds the idea geometrically with animations before any formulas.
Ip3X9LOh2dk.why: HN repeatedly points people to it as the clearest visual intuition for determinants, often saying it finally made the concept click.

IV3dnLzthDA.summary: Veritasium tells the story of Thomas Midgley Jr., who introduced leaded gasoline and CFCs, and covers the science behind lead exposure and ozone damage. It also touches on isotope geochemistry used to uncover the history.
IV3dnLzthDA.why: HN commenters recommend it whenever leaded fuel, toxic chemicals or corporate profit motives come up, praising its storytelling and accessible science.

IeTybKL1pM4.summary: Nina Paley's one-minute animated free culture anthem with vocals by Connie Champagne, arguing that copying is not theft.
IeTybKL1pM4.why: Linked constantly in copyright and piracy debates as a short explainer of the difference between copying and physical theft.

IAF8DjrQSSk.summary: Fons van der Plas introduces Pluto.jl, a reactive notebook for Julia that tracks references between cells and re-runs affected cells when code changes. The talk was given at JuliaCon 2020.
IAF8DjrQSSk.why: HN recommends it as an enthusiastic demo of spreadsheet-like reactive notebooks, which commenters think new notebook projects should copy.

IRTfhkiAqPw.summary: Brian Will follows up his earlier anti-OOP video by walking through four short code examples, including Java code in the style of Uncle Bob, to show how object-oriented design complicates simple programs. It argues that OOP hides and scatters state and adds needless indirection.
IRTfhkiAqPw.why: HN commenters point to it as a sharp, example-driven critique of OOP and Clean Code style, often alongside Brian Will's other anti-OO videos.

ISAKc9gpGjw.summary: Utah State plant scientist Bruce Bugbee presents his analysis of the energy and environmental costs of vertical and indoor farming. He argues artificial lighting cannot compete with sunlight in fields or greenhouses.
ISAKc9gpGjw.why: HN uses it as the go-to rebuttal to vertical farming hype, since it gives hard numbers from a leading controlled-environment authority.

IgF3OX8nT0w.summary: Veritasium traces analog computers from the Antikythera mechanism and Kelvin's tide-predicting machines to fire control and modern analog approaches. It explains how these machines computed continuously rather than digitally.
IgF3OX8nT0w.why: Recommended in threads on analog computing, photonic chips, AI hardware and tide prediction as an engaging history of Kelvin's machines.

I7IdS-PbEgI.summary: Lee Byron of Facebook explains how persistent immutable data structures work and how to use them in React apps with Immutable.js. He covers memoization benefits and avoiding coupling through shared mutable state.
I7IdS-PbEgI.why: HN points to it as a clear explanation of immutable data structures such as tries, and of the case for immutability with React and Flux.

If61baWF4GE.summary: RealLifeLore explains with maps why Russia invaded Ukraine, focusing on energy resources, security buffers, Black Sea access and Crimea's strategic value.
If61baWF4GE.why: HN users shared it during the early 2022 invasion as a clear, map-driven overview of Russia's economic and strategic motives.

IroPQ150F6c.summary: Andrew Kelley, creator of Zig, presents practical data-oriented design techniques for shrinking memory footprint and making programs cache friendly. He ends with a case study of how these ideas sped up the Zig compiler.
IroPQ150F6c.why: HN cites it as one of the best talks on data-oriented design, applying struct-of-arrays and compact data layouts to a real compiler.

IS5ycm7VfXg.summary: Sam Zeloof shows the upgraded second iteration of his homemade silicon integrated circuit fabrication process, producing chips with around a thousand transistors in his garage. It is a short overview of what the home fab can now do.
IS5ycm7VfXg.why: HN uses it as the go-to proof that small-scale, hobbyist chip fabrication is real, and as an entry point to the topic.

Imquk_3oFf4.summary: Memories is a 256-byte MS-DOS demo that packs eight effects and MIDI soundscapes into a tiny program. It won first place at Revision 2020.
Imquk_3oFf4.why: HN people share it as a mind-blowing example of demoscene craft and the reigning champion of 256-byte demos.

IrbJYsep45E.summary: A PBS Infinite Series episode explaining the mathematics of quantum computers, including how qubits store complex numbers and how quantum computation differs from classical computation. Hosted by Kelsey Houston-Edwards.
IrbJYsep45E.why: HN recommends it as one of the most accessible yet accurate introductions to quantum computing, and part of a wider series that covers Shor's algorithm.

IRVdiHu1VCc.summary: Mike Rowe, host of Dirty Jobs, shares stories from messy real-world jobs in this TED talk. He argues that hard work has been unjustly degraded in society.
IRVdiHu1VCc.why: It comes up in threads on career choice, trades, handiness and the 'follow your passion' advice.

IUDTlvagjJA.summary: A binaural audio demo, the 'Virtual Barber Shop', that places a barber moving around your head. It works best with headphones and closed eyes.
IUDTlvagjJA.why: It is the classic demo HN people point to for showing positional 3D audio working on ordinary headphones.

Ilg3gGewQ5U.summary: 3Blue1Brown's third deep learning chapter gives a visual, intuitive account of backpropagation and what happens to a neural network as it learns. A follow-up video covers the underlying calculus.
Ilg3gGewQ5U.why: Recommended as the most accessible introduction to backprop for people who struggle with the pure math.

I6xwMIUPHss.summary: BobbyBroccoli documentary on the rise of Nortel Networks, once the dominant Canadian telecom giant, during the dot-com era. It is part one of a two-part story.
I6xwMIUPHss.why: Recommended as a well-made documentary explaining Nortel's rise and the index-fund and bubble dynamics around it.

IHZwWFHWa-w.summary: 3Blue1Brown's second neural network chapter explains cost functions and gradient descent, showing how a network learns by minimizing error during training.
IHZwWFHWa-w.why: HN recommends the series as a very accessible way to understand the math behind machine learning and LLMs.

IJcuQQ1eWWI.summary: Soren Johnson, a lead designer and AI programmer on Civilization games, discusses game AI design, including whether AI should cheat, behave like a human or be fun rather than strong. He uses the Civilization series as a case study.
IJcuQQ1eWWI.why: HN commenters recommend it as the key talk on why game AI is built to be fun rather than to win.

IJiHDmyhE1A.summary: The official video for Baba Yetu, Christopher Tin's Swahili-language choral piece written as the theme to Civilization IV. It was the first video game music to win a Grammy.
IJiHDmyhE1A.why: HN commenters hold it up as the greatest video game song, evoking wonder and pride in humanity.

IX-gTobCJHs.summary: A concept video from Nokia Research Center and Cambridge Nanoscience Center showing Morph, a flexible, self-cleaning, shape-changing phone imagined through nanotechnology.
IX-gTobCJHs.why: HN brings it up as a nostalgic, exciting concept in threads on foldable phones and design, and sometimes as an example of concept videos that never shipped.

IaWdEtANi-0.summary: An Al Jazeera English People & Power investigation from 2010 into safety problems with the Boeing 737NG, featuring whistleblowers on cracking parts, hand-made structural components and an alleged cover-up.
IaWdEtANi-0.why: HN resurfaces it during Boeing safety stories as early, firsthand evidence that production and management problems long predate the 737 Max.

IeSu_odkI5I.summary: Armin Ronacher's EuroPython 2017 keynote examining how the CPython interpreter's leaky abstractions affect language design and how Python could evolve, drawing on JavaScript and Rust experience.
IeSu_odkI5I.why: Recommended for explaining why Python is hard to optimize and the limits of making it fast.

IkdziSLYzHw.summary: Geoffrey Hinton's 2025 Royal Institution Discourse on what AI has learned from biological intelligence and how it might surpass it. He explains neural networks and argues that human language use resembles what backpropagation-trained networks do.
IkdziSLYzHw.why: HN readers recommend it as an intuitive explanation of neural networks that shifts how people think about AI and language.

ImoQqNyRL8Y.summary: Smarter Every Day shares a binaural audio recording of the SpaceX Falcon Heavy launch made by Trevor Mahlmann, with explanations of the sounds including the sonic booms of the landing boosters. It is meant to be heard with headphones.
ImoQqNyRL8Y.why: Recommended in launch threads as an immersive way to hear what a Falcon Heavy launch actually sounds like.

Iod6uwUGM2E.summary: Jared Owen's 3D animated breakdown of how a Brunswick GS-X bowling pinsetter works, showing its mechanisms for sweeping, lifting and resetting pins and balls.
Iod6uwUGM2E.why: HN recommends it as an exceptionally well-made explainer of complex mechanical machinery.

IrabKK9Bhds.summary: The trailer for Peter Jackson's They Shall Not Grow Old, a WWI documentary built from restored, colorized archival footage and BBC interviews with British soldiers.
IrabKK9Bhds.why: HN points to it as a way to see WWI footage restored so the war feels modern and real.

IxuU5L2MEII.summary: George Hotz of Comma AI gives a 2017 conference talk on lessons from building a self-driving system. He argues about how driving should be defined and why the common approach to autonomous vehicles is flawed.
IxuU5L2MEII.why: HN commenters point to it as a candid, contrarian view of self-driving approaches and the real limits of the business.

Iyp_X3mwE1w.summary: Technology Connections' hour-long guide to electric vehicles, covering costs, trade-offs and especially how little home charging power most drivers need.
Iyp_X3mwE1w.why: Recommended as an entertaining, in-depth beginner's guide that persuades skeptics that a wall outlet often suffices.

I845O57ZSy4.summary: A five-hour Lex Fridman interview with John Carmack covering Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, programming, games and rockets.
I845O57ZSy4.why: HN mines it for Carmack's views on AGI, debuggers, tooling and the metaverse, and recommends it as worth the full length.

ILNs1GChGDk.summary: A BSidesLV 2013 talk from the Sixteen Colors project on archiving the ANSI and ASCII art scene. It traces the scene's evolution from BBSs to the NFO and IRC era.
ILNs1GChGDk.why: Commenters recommend it as the best introduction to the history of the ANSI and ASCII art scene.

IRG-YubP1rw.summary: A Harvard Business Review video with tactics for getting better at small talk and enjoying it, such as setting goals, allowing pauses, and starting and ending conversations.
IRG-YubP1rw.why: HN commenters share it as a short, practical resource for people who struggle with small talk.

IYO3tOqDISE.summary: A short film from the Competitive Enterprise Institute adapting Leonard Read's 1958 essay I, Pencil, showing how no one person knows how to make a pencil and how many people cooperate without central planning.
IYO3tOqDISE.why: HN recommends it as a quick video version of the classic essay on specialization and economic interdependence.

Ie-gqwSHQr0.summary: Matthew Griffith, creator of elm-ui, presents a toolkit for designing layouts in Elm as an alternative to CSS. He explains the opinionated approach to layout and styling.
Ie-gqwSHQr0.why: HN commenters recommend it as a fresh perspective on layout and styling in CSS discussions.

Ijst4g5KFN0.summary: MIT 22.01 lecture by Michael Short explaining the Chernobyl accident technically, including RBMK reactor positive feedback, xenon poisoning and the cascade of human errors during the test.
Ijst4g5KFN0.why: Recommended as the detailed technical account of exactly what happened at Chernobyl.

Iq9DzN6mvYA.summary: Jake Vanderplas's PyCon 2016 talk shows how sampling-based methods such as simulation, shuffling and bootstrapping make statistics intuitive. His pitch is that if you can write a for-loop, you can do statistics.
Iq9DzN6mvYA.why: It is recommended to programmers who want to learn statistics through simulation rather than memorized formulas.

I4flQ8XdvJM.summary: Dave Ackley presents robust-first computing and the ULAM programming language for the Movable Feast Machine, a cellular-automata-like architecture. It was a short video for the Future Programming Workshop 2015.
I4flQ8XdvJM.why: HN points to it as an entry into Ackley's indefinitely scalable computing project, with a network-switch demo recommended as the best place to start.

IHD8BDFYyGI.summary: Patrick Boyle analyzes SpaceX's IPO prospectus, covering its financials, speculative products, AI business, related-party dealings, compensation, and a governance structure with minimal shareholder rights.
IHD8BDFYyGI.why: Recommended as a clear, roughly 30-minute summary of the problems with the SpaceX IPO.

IQZ_bQbxSXk.summary: A Stanford EE380 seminar by Michael P. Frank of Sandia National Laboratories on generalized reversible computing. It surveys unconventional computing approaches as transistor scaling nears its limits and energy efficiency stops improving.
IQZ_bQbxSXk.why: HN commenters cite it as an informative talk from a leading researcher in reversible computing, mainly in threads on reversible computers and energy efficiency.

ISptt3CRAqc.summary: Psychologist Irving Kirsch gives a distinguished lecture on antidepressant trials and the placebo effect. He argues drug-placebo differences are small outside severe depression.
ISptt3CRAqc.why: HN points to it in discussions of antidepressant efficacy, the serotonin model and the power of placebos.

Ii_pEXKKYUg.summary: Chris Celio of UC Berkeley compares the RISC-V, ARM and x86 instruction sets, with quantitative data on instruction counts and code density. It examines how the compressed extension fares against Thumb and x86.
Ii_pEXKKYUg.why: Cited as primary-source evidence that RISC-V code density is competitive with or better than ARM and x86.

IsE_8j5RL3k.summary: Dialect coach Erik Singer tours a range of accents across North America with linguists in Part 2 of WIRED's accent series. It covers regional distinctions such as Southern Mississippi, Miami and Utah English.
IsE_8j5RL3k.why: HN commenters recommend it as an enjoyable, accessible tour of US accents and cite it in threads on vowel shifts and dialects.

I3l4XLZ59iw.summary: Adobe's VoCo demo from the MAX 2016 Sneak Peeks, co-hosted by Jordan Peele, showing software that changes words in a voiceover by typing new ones.
I3l4XLZ59iw.why: HN cites it as the early example of voice cloning and audio deepfakes, with some recommending Peele's reaction and others calling the demo fake or never shipped.

I6IQ_FOCE6I.summary: A cappella parody song by The Richter Scales, set to Billy Joel's 'We Didn't Start the Fire', lampooning the Web 2.0 startup bubble. It won a Webby for viral video in 2007.
I6IQ_FOCE6I.why: Resurfaces in threads on startups, valuations and hype cycles as a funny, prescient bubble satire.

ICp2-EUKQAI.summary: KRAZAM parody sketch in which an Excel streamer, Makro, treats the XLOOKUP function as a game-breaking meta change, spoofing e-sports commentary.
ICp2-EUKQAI.why: Shared in Excel threads as a funny parody that treats spreadsheets like an e-sport.

IDgDWbQtlKI.summary: A VPRO documentary following ecologist and cameraman John D. Liu. He documents the regreening of China's Loess Plateau and other efforts to restore deserts and biodiversity around the world.
IDgDWbQtlKI.why: HN cites it as the best-documented example of landscape-scale restoration working, with striking before and after footage from the Loess Plateau.

IE7j1SgUpKs.summary: A Ropecon 2019 talk by a lighting designer and a software engineer on how the Odysseus larp spaceship was built, using over ten IT systems, hundreds of lights and dozens of speakers. It covers the lessons learned.
IE7j1SgUpKs.why: HN people share it as a look at the custom backend and hardware behind a large sci-fi larp.

IOs6hnTI4lw.summary: Recording of Steve Jobs's 1997 Macworld Boston keynote, in which he reviews Apple's status and announces the partnership with Microsoft, including a $150 million investment and a five-year Office commitment. The audience reaction is part of the draw.
IOs6hnTI4lw.why: HN shares it for a firsthand view of Apple's near-bankruptcy moment and the crowd's booing of the Microsoft deal.

IQJL3htsDyQ.summary: Mark Rober tests whether self-driving cars can be fooled, comparing a lidar-equipped car with a camera-only Tesla in scenarios including a painted Wile E. Coyote wall and smoke.
IQJL3htsDyQ.why: HN uses it as the reference demonstration in lidar versus camera debates, though some critics fault its methodology and style.

IS3i3DTUnAI.summary: A Clojure/conj 2019 talk by Wilker Silva on how namespace-qualified keywords and context-free federated names can be used pragmatically for data modeling, drawn from his experience at Nubank. It builds toward a graph-based view of connecting data from many sources.
IS3i3DTUnAI.why: Cited as a demonstration of the Pathom/graph approach to connecting APIs, as an alternative to GraphQL.

ITTxTCz4Ums.summary: Sam Harris's talk at the 2012 Global Atheist Convention on the secular attitude toward death and living in the present moment, with a guided meditation element.
ITTxTCz4Ums.why: HN commenters point to it as a liberating account of present-moment awareness and mindfulness.

IZmaeC_Ma5A.summary: Photopea founder Ivan Kutskir talks about developing a free browser-based photo editor, one of the most complex JavaScript programs ever written, and the web technologies behind it.
IZmaeC_Ma5A.why: HN points to it as a look under the hood of a remarkable one-developer project.

IdpD5QIVOKQ.summary: Jonathan Blow's LambdaConf 2025 keynote demonstrates the Jai programming language and explains its design. It includes demos of metaprogramming and tools that visualize programs.
IdpD5QIVOKQ.why: HN points to it for seeing Jai's compile-time metaprogramming in practice and for Blow's tools that visualize programs to spot problems.

IiuVggWNqSA.summary: Second half of a 2017 Computer History Museum live event in which former Apple software chief Scott Forstall is interviewed by John Markoff about creating the original iPhone. He tells stories about Steve Jobs and the team and the origins of the iPhone software.
IiuVggWNqSA.why: HN commenters cite it for Forstall's firsthand anecdotes and his account of how the iPhone came about.

IjJmTeBSEzU.summary: Last Day of War is an award-winning CGI animated short by Dima Fedotov in which automated machines keep following orders and prepare a bomber after all humans are dead.
IjJmTeBSEzU.why: HN cites it in threads on military AI as a vivid depiction of where autonomous warfare could lead.

IoL8g0W9gAQ.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on the US Postal Service's financial troubles. John Oliver explains why it matters, what pushed it to this point, and what viewers can do.
IoL8g0W9gAQ.why: HN points to it as an accessible explanation of why the USPS struggles financially, especially in threads on mail delays and international rates.

IvUU8joBb1Q.summary: Wintergatan's video of the Marble Machine, a hand-built music instrument that plays a song using about 2000 marbles on a mechanical clockwork-style mechanism.
IvUU8joBb1Q.why: HN treats it as the canonical example of a Rube Goldberg style musical instrument and a work of love, and references it in threads on unconventional instruments and machines.

I9LZ6TnSP40.summary: A 12-minute demo of the Alternate Reality Kit, built by Randall Smith at Xerox PARC in 1986. It is a simulated physical world in which users manipulate objects and program by direct interaction.
I9LZ6TnSP40.why: HN cites it as early evidence that visual and interactive programming can go well beyond wire diagrams, in a Smalltalk and Alan Kay tradition.

IQPsKvG6WMI.summary: A short clip of former KGB defector Yuri Bezmenov in 1984 describing Soviet ideological subversion of Western societies. It is a political commentary excerpt from his longer lecture.
IQPsKvG6WMI.why: HN commenters cite it in political and disinformation threads as a source on Soviet psychological operations, a contested claim.

I14b-C67EXY.summary: A short compilation of Steve Ballmer energetically shouting and dancing on stage at Microsoft events, including the famous developers chant.
I14b-C67EXY.why: HN commenters use it as a joke or shorthand for the developers chant, mostly not as a recommendation.

IA7REQxohV4.summary: The 8-Bit Guy reviews the Color Maximite 2, a modern ARM-based computer that boots straight into BASIC. He shows what it can do as a retro-style machine.
IA7REQxohV4.why: It is cited as a review of a new boot-to-BASIC computer, and one commenter suggests it for a kid starting to program.

IESEcsjDcmM.summary: A compilation of the hacking scenes from the 1995 film Hackers, featuring flashy visualizations of computer intrusion.
IESEcsjDcmM.why: HN mostly cites it for humor, with one commenter arguing the visuals work as a representation of what goes on in a programmer's mind.

IFe9wiDfb0E.summary: Tom Scott's three-minute satirical short about a corporate-run, DRM-and-ads-laden afterlife after mind uploading. It imagines copyright law and lawyers applied to human memory and consciousness.
IFe9wiDfb0E.why: HN cites it as dystopian satire in threads on DRM, digital ownership, mind uploading and AI copyright, often noting it increasingly looks like reality.

II2QF9JwtLc.summary: Louis Rossmann explains how Google delisted his repair business site for almost a year, and how having AI rewrite his authentic content into corporate-style text finally restored his rankings.
II2QF9JwtLc.why: HN cites it as a firsthand example of search engines rewarding AI-flavored content over genuine writing.

IJ-a2KeyCAY.summary: CNN's clip of Stephen Colbert's 2006 White House Correspondents' Dinner routine, in which he mocks President Bush and the press in character. It was republished on the tenth anniversary.
IJ-a2KeyCAY.why: HN cites it as the source of the line that reality has a liberal bias and as a performance people still find phenomenal.

IJEaMtNN_dM.summary: Tom Scott explains Gricean maxims, the unwritten guidelines that shape how we understand each other. He uses examples such as why 'asbestos-free cereal' sounds suspicious.
IJEaMtNN_dM.why: HN uses it as a short, clear explanation of implied meaning in conversation and the cooperative principle.

IJNR2EpS0jw.summary: The viral Dumb Ways to Die music video, a cheerful animated song created for a Melbourne rail safety campaign. It lists absurd ways to die and ends with warnings about trains.
IJNR2EpS0jw.why: HN mentions it mostly as a joke or a pop-culture reference, and as the campaign that titles play on.

IKqXu-5jw60.summary: The 1951 US civil defense film 'Duck and Cover', starring Bert the Turtle, which taught schoolchildren to drop and shield themselves during a nuclear attack. It was shown to millions of children and is preserved in the National Film Registry.
IKqXu-5jw60.why: HN uses it as an example of Cold War fear and persuasion, with some defending the advice as sensible against blast debris and others mocking it.

ILQepXUhJ98.summary: A five-minute clip of a George Carlin routine arguing that the education system is designed to produce compliant citizens rather than critical thinkers. It ties schooling to the interests of the people who own the country.
ILQepXUhJ98.why: HN links it as a pointed comedic statement of why education is seen as broken and unlikely to be fixed.

IRn4xzaugbk.summary: A Rare Earth explainer on Japan's criminal justice system and its extremely high conviction rate. It outlines the system's idiosyncrasies and how suspects are treated.
IRn4xzaugbk.why: HN cites it in threads about Japan's near-total conviction rate and what it says about the culture and legal system.

IUK6zjtUj00.summary: A live 2007 performance of Todd Snider's song 'Statistician's Blues' at the Great American Music Hall. The song satirizes statistics and how readily people believe them.
IUK6zjtUj00.why: It is mostly cited as a joke or a wry reference in threads about dubious statistics.

Iuv6hY6zsd0.summary: Veritasium revisits Thomas Young's original double slit experiment with light, showing how interference supports the wave nature of light. It uses a pond-wave demonstration to explain the pattern.
Iuv6hY6zsd0.why: HN cites it in double slit debates for its grounded demonstration of interference as classical wave behavior.

I25UeVXrEHQ.summary: A short clip from a lecture Q&A in which Richard Stallman appears to pick something off his foot and eat it.
I25UeVXrEHQ.why: Used as a recurring gag or jab at Stallman's social eccentricities; not recommended for its content.

I39sxwYKlEE.summary: A three-minute Computer History Museum clip showing Ernst Dickmanns' VaMoRs Mercedes van and later VaMP sedan, early self-driving vehicles tested from 1986 to 2003.
I39sxwYKlEE.why: HN cites it as footage proving that autonomous driving was demonstrated in Europe decades before the current wave.

I9lquok4Pdk.summary: A timeline visualization plotting the 2053 nuclear tests and detonations from 1945 to 1998 on a world map, with sound marking each blast. It conveys the pace of the nuclear arms race.
I9lquok4Pdk.why: HN links it as a reference for the history and distribution of nuclear tests, and occasionally as an example of audio data presentation.

IACHfKmZMr8.summary: A Y Combinator video on vibe coding, the term Andrej Karpathy coined for letting LLMs write code. It reports what YC founders say about debugging, models and how much of their code is AI-written.
IACHfKmZMr8.why: HN mostly cites it critically, as a source for the claim that much of YC code is AI-written and as an example of insiders promoting vibe coding.

IBrEx-FINEI.summary: A brief toast by lithography expert Chris Mack at SPIE Advanced Lithography 2014, humorously declaring the end of Moore's Law. His argument centers on the cost per transistor no longer falling.
IBrEx-FINEI.why: HN cites it when arguing Moore's Law is really about price per transistor and that this economic trend has stalled.

IFACrIx5SZ0.summary: Short BBC Earth clip from Life of Mammals in which David Attenborough shows orangutans imitating human behaviors like washing clothes with soap and using tools.
IFACrIx5SZ0.why: Linked as a quick demonstration of orangutans copying human tool use and chores.

IKVFZ28ybQs.summary: A StarCraft 2 custom-map demo where a bot controls 100 zerglings against 20 sieged tanks and dodges the splash damage, leaving 19 survivors. The code was written in Blizzard's World Editor.
IKVFZ28ybQs.why: Cited in StarCraft and AI threads as a vivid example of superhuman micro and of machine speed advantage over humans.

IRELLH86Edo.summary: Clip from The Dark Knight in which Batman uses a sonar-based system that turns phones into a city-wide surveillance network.
IRELLH86Edo.why: Used as a pop-culture analogy for mass surveillance technology that now looks plausible.

ISznqY3kESI.summary: A short Boston Dynamics demo of RHex, a 30-lb six-legged robot built for rough terrain, remotely operated with a video uplink and about four hours of battery life. It can run right-side-up or upside-down.
ISznqY3kESI.why: Mentioned in passing as an example of practical legged robots and as a comparison point for hexapod projects.

IVpOyKCNZYw.summary: A two-minute clip of Linus Torvalds at an Aalto University talk telling Nvidia "F_ck you" over its poor Linux support. It is an excerpt of a longer talk.
IVpOyKCNZYw.why: HN cites it as shorthand for the long-running frustration of the Linux community with Nvidia's drivers, often as a joke or background.

IW7Rqwwth84.summary: A very short clip of Bill Gates hitting a Blue Screen of Death while demonstrating plug and play on Windows 98 on stage.
IW7Rqwwth84.why: HN cites it as the classic demo failure, in threads about USB, plug and play, and Microsoft's shipping quality.

IWkNkQoQY_8.summary: A short archival capture of the 2001 Flash website of 2Advanced Studios, an agency known for high-end Flash design. It is part of the Web Design Museum's collection of early web design.
IWkNkQoQY_8.why: HN commenters link it as nostalgic proof of how inventive and formative the Flash-era web was.

IX_d_vMKswE.summary: A sketch from the British sitcom Yes, Prime Minister in which Jim Hacker and the chief scientific advisor discuss the logic of the nuclear deterrent.
IX_d_vMKswE.why: HN commenters cite it as a funny but precise take on deterrence strategy and politics.

IaO69CF5mbY.summary: A two-minute clip of Richard Feynman on the social sciences, discussing what counts as real science versus pseudo science.
